newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Bank SinoPac to buy U.S. bank for $85m.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Bank SinoPac to buy U.S. bank for $85m.

text.p: Taiwan's Bank SinoPac said it signed a deal on Thursday to buy Far East National Bank of California for about US$84.7 million.
"We just signed the deal this morning to buy all the equity of Far East National Bank," Sinopac said in a statement.
A SinoPac spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone the purchase value wouild be 1.925 times that of Far East National's net asset value, or about US$84.7 million.
Far East National has a total assets of US$500 million with a net asset value of US$44 million, although the figure was subject to change through the acquisition, the buyer said.
"Its net asset value may change when we complete the deal," the spokeswoman said.
The SinoPac statement said applications for approvals would be submitted soon and if U.S. and Taiwan regulators allow the deal, the acquisition would be completed in 1997.
Sinopac, with 24 branches on Taiwan, has reached total assets of T$110 billion, it said.

The spokeswoman said the deal will help Sinopac, which is partly owned by Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, to enter the mainland China market because Far East National has a representative office in Beijing.
Sinopac, therefore, would become the first Taiwanese bank to enter China market.

Taiwan has prohibited direct contact with mainland Chinese government and financial bodies since the Chinese Nationalist government, vanquished by the Chinese communists, fled into exile on Taiwan in 1949.

In mid-1995, Taipei began permitting indirect contacts with China's banks, allowing some Taiwan banks and offshore banking units do business with the overseas branches of Chinese banks so long as they routed their business through a third territory.
